title: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has initiated a significant emergency food drop operation in southern Sudan to combat severe famine affecting up to 1.2 million people. Four Hercules C-130 planes are delivering food to 40 sites in the Bhar el Ghazal province, with plans to increase monthly food deliveries from 6,500 to 9,600 tonnes. The operation faces challenges due to ongoing civil conflict, logistical difficulties, and a lack of cooperation from the Sudanese government. Despite these hurdles, WFP aims to support local communities in resuming food cultivation. However, funding shortfalls and potential disruptions from the rainy season pose ongoing concerns for the operation's sustainability.
